name: Edificio Telefónica

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/192107181 (centroid of the outline; long axis at 95.8°, the Gran Vía front faces 185.8°)

rights.note: Designed by Ignacio de Cárdenas Pastor for the Compañía Telefónica Nacional de España, built 1926–1929 (steel frame, Novelda limestone over a granite base). The architect died in 1979; under Spanish law authors who died before December 1987 are protected for 80 years after death: free in 2060.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q2092717_edificio_telefonica.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The massing is the OpenStreetMap building:part pieces extruded to their heights: the 28–32 m ring on the three streets (8–9 floors, Baroque crests on its parapet), the set-back ring at 43 m, the core at 50 m, lift pavilions at 53 m, the 11 m light court, the tower on the Gran Vía axis (14 × 14 m) to 73 m and the clock stage (9 × 9 m) to the quoted 89 m at the top of its crest and finial. The thin 46 m strip OSM puts in front of the tower is taken as the tower's own front (the photos show the tower flush with the street), a tiny 46 m triangle at the back as 43 m. Granite base 0–9 m (shop floor and mezzanine), floors of 3.4 m above; windows are dark quads on a ~3.2 m grid; the Baroque portal, the shield (no crown), the clock faces (on all four sides), crests, pinnacles, corner pilasters and cornices are stylised. No signs or logos: the shop fronts are plain dark glazing; the antennas (removed in 2017) are not modelled. Uncertain: the vertical split of the tower above 53 m — on some photos the shaft looks only a couple of floors higher than the core, which would put the crown lower than 89 m; the OSM heights and the published 89 m were kept. The back (north) façades are shown plainer and slightly darker, as on the photos, without checking their real window pattern.
